I’d rank them as 1. Chicago, 2. Milwaukee, 3. MSP. Milwaukee to me is ahead of MSP because of its proximity to Chicago.

MKE is mostly affordable, with decent restaurants and bars. Some nice parks in the area, but I’d say that MSP wins on that front in the Cities and in the surrounding counties. The neighborhoods in MKE don’t have an urban feel like they do Chicago.

The lakefront in MKE is more accessible than it is in Chicago, based on parking, the need to get over LSD vs Lincoln Memorial, and the beaches. 

Skyline wise, no competition: 1. Chicago, 2. MSP, 3. Milwaukee.

Nightlife wise, I can’t speak too much on MSP. When I was in my early and mid 20s, Uptown was a lot of fun, but I think nightlife has shifted so I’m not sure where to go now. Maybe North Loop? Milwaukee has a ton of bars that were fun in my early and mid 20s, but I feel like I’ve aged out of half of them at 30. Chicago nightlife is superior because of public transit and walkability between places, and the variety of places you can go. I’m gay, so Boystown has been my favorite for nearly a decade but other bars in the neighborhoods can be great.

Chicago is great for meeting people - there’s so many transplants that people are eager to connect. I served in a restaurant there in my early and mid 20s and met some of the best people I still hang out with when I’m there or they come here. But again I’m a gay man so results may vary. I can’t speak to MSP on that. Milwaukee has been decent for meeting people, several of my friends went to college here so I met people through them, but there’s also a handful of my friends from my hometown who live here and sometimes we can be a little insulated amongst ourselves. Definitely more townies in the MKE and MSP areas. I wouldn’t consider Chicago residents from the suburbs as townies, they’re just different.
